1	"""
2	Video-based fret detection -- camera pointed at the game screen.
3	
4	Consumes frames from the shared reference video buffer (camera.py); does
5	not own the camera. Sensor markers and per-button signal levels are
6	exposed as an overlay layer through the `overlays()` hook so the server
7	can bake them into the live MJPEG and paused scrub frames.
8	
9	Two sensor points per button, both above the strike line:
10	
11	  Sensor 1 (hold)  -- brightness detect (color OR white).
12	                      Sets pressed=True whenever anything bright appears.
13	  Sensor 2 (edge)  -- color-filtered leading-edge detect.
14	                      Increments press_count on each new note arrival,
15	                      which the actuator uses to schedule strums.
16	
17	Use video_calibrate.py to find pixel coordinates for all 10 sensor
18	points. Detection thresholds are applied to raw pixel values (dark
19	background is the implicit zero).
20	
21	The "baseline" output is the stronger of the two signals (scaled to
22	0..4095) for chart overlay visualization.
23	
24	Requires: opencv-python
25	"""
26	
27	import threading
28	from typing import Optional
29	
30	import cv2
31	import numpy as np
32	
33	from camera import Frame, get_camera
34	from stream import CH_COLORS, CHANNELS, Sample, make_slot_schema
35	
36	_DIST_SCALE = 4095.0 / 255.0  # map max single-channel distance (255) to 0..4095
37	
38	# Per-button color filter for the edge detector (sensor 2).
39	# (target_weights, reject_weights) in BGR order.
40	# Detection signal = target - reject.  Reject weights > 1.0 total
41	# so that camera-captured whites (which have color-temperature bias)
42	# are aggressively suppressed, not just mathematically-perfect whites.
43	_COLOR_FILTER: dict[str, tuple[tuple[float, ...], tuple[float, ...]]] = {
44	    "green":  ((0, 1, 0),     (0.7, 0, 0.7)),   # want G up, penalize B/R
45	    "red":    ((0, 0, 1),     (0.7, 0.7, 0)),    # want R up, penalize B/G
46	    "yellow": ((0, 0.5, 0.5), (1.4, 0, 0)),      # want R+G up, penalize B
47	    "blue":   ((1, 0.4, 0),   (0, 0, 1.4)),       # want B + some G, penalize R
48	    "orange": ((0, 0.3, 0.7), (1.4, 0, 0)),      # want R+someG up, penalize B
49	}
50	
51	_MARKER_COLORS = {
52	    "green":  (0, 200, 0),
53	    "red":    (0, 0, 220),
54	    "yellow": (0, 220, 220),
55	    "blue":   (220, 0, 0),
56	    "orange": (0, 140, 255),
57	}
58	_IDLE_COLOR = (120, 120, 120)
59	_PRESSED_COLOR = (0, 255, 0)
60	
61	_MARKER_RADIUS = 16
62	_MARKER_THICK = 3
63	_FONT_SCALE = 0.6
64	_FONT_THICK = 2
65	
66	# Calibration coords are anchored to a 1920x1080 reference frame.
67	_CAL_W = 1920
68	_CAL_H = 1080
69	
70	
71	class Detector:
72	    """Camera-based fret press detector consuming the shared video buffer."""
73	
74	    @classmethod
75	    def default_params(cls) -> dict:
76	        return {

78	            "HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC": 60,
79	            "EDGE_GREEN": 50,
80	            "EDGE_RED": 50,
81	            "EDGE_YELLOW": 50,
82	            "EDGE_BLUE": 50,
83	            "EDGE_ORANGE": 50,
84	            "PATCH_RADIUS": 2,
85	            "GREEN_X": 748, "GREEN_Y": 700,
86	            "RED_X": 850, "RED_Y": 700,
87	            "YELLOW_X": 947, "YELLOW_Y": 700,
88	            "BLUE_X": 1045, "BLUE_Y": 700,
89	            "ORANGE_X": 1147, "ORANGE_Y": 700,
90	            "GREEN_EX": 780, "GREEN_EY": 700,
91	            "RED_EX": 882, "RED_EY": 700,
92	            "YELLOW_EX": 979, "YELLOW_EY": 700,
93	            "BLUE_EX": 1013, "BLUE_EY": 700,
94	            "ORANGE_EX": 1115, "ORANGE_EY": 700,
95	        }

97	    def __init__(self, **params):
98	        defaults = self.default_params()
99	        defaults.update(params)
100	
101	        self._hold_thresh = int(defaults["HOLD_THRESH"])
102	        self._hold_release = self._hold_thresh * int(defaults["HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC"]) // 100
103	        self._edge_thresh: dict[str, int] = {
104	            ch: int(defaults[f"EDGE_{ch.upper()}"]) for ch in CHANNELS
105	        }
106	        self._patch_r = max(0, int(defaults["PATCH_RADIUS"]))
107	
108	        self._cal_hold_pixels: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
109	        self._cal_edge_pixels: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
110	        for ch in CHANNELS:
111	            p = ch.upper()
112	            self._cal_hold_pixels[ch] = (int(defaults[f"{p}_X"]), int(defaults[f"{p}_Y"]))
113	            self._cal_edge_pixels[ch] = (int(defaults[f"{p}_EX"]), int(defaults[f"{p}_EY"]))
114	
115	        # Per-frame-size cache of scaled pixel coords. The capture path
116	        # passes full-res frames to detection while the view path applies
117	        # overlays onto the downscaled working frame, so we typically need
118	        # at least two entries (one for detection, one for view). Callers
119	        # treat the returned dicts as immutable.
120	        self._scaled_cache: dict[
121	            tuple[int, int],
122	            tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, int]], dict[str, tuple[int, int]]],
123	        ] = {}
124	        self._scale_lock = threading.Lock()
125	
126	        self._hold_dist: dict[str, float] = {ch: 0.0 for ch in CHANNELS}
127	        self._edge_dist: dict[str, float] = {ch: 0.0 for ch in CHANNELS}
128	        self._pressed: dict[str, bool] = {ch: False for ch in CHANNELS}
129	        self._press_count: dict[str, int] = {ch: 0 for ch in CHANNELS}
130	        self._edge_active: dict[str, bool] = {ch: False for ch in CHANNELS}
131	        self._cached_result: Optional[dict] = None
132	
133	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
134	
135	        self._cam = get_camera()
136	        self._cam.add_frame_listener(self._on_frame)
137	
138	    def stop(self):
139	        """Detach the camera frame listener."""
140	        try:
141	            self._cam.remove_frame_listener(self._on_frame)
142	        except Exception:
143	            pass
144	        self._log("stopped")
145	
146	    def __del__(self):
147	        try:
148	            self._cam.remove_frame_listener(self._on_frame)
149	        except Exception:
150	            pass
151	
152	    def _log(self, msg: str):
153	        print(f"[detect_video] {msg}", flush=True)
154	
155	    _EDGE_RADIUS = 10
156	    _EDGE_THICK = 2
157	
158	    def _scale_pixels(
159	        self, frame_w: int, frame_h: int,
160	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, int]], dict[str, tuple[int, int]]]:
161	        """Return (hold_pixels, edge_pixels) scaled for the given frame size.
162	
163	        Cached per (w, h) so the detection (full-res) and overlay (working-res)
164	        paths don't keep invalidating each other. Returned dicts are shared
165	        across calls and should be treated as immutable by callers.
166	        """
167	        key = (frame_w, frame_h)
168	        with self._scale_lock:
169	            cached = self._scaled_cache.get(key)
170	            if cached is not None:
171	                return cached
172	
173	            all_cal = list(self._cal_hold_pixels.values()) + list(self._cal_edge_pixels.values())
174	            cal_xs = [x for x, _ in all_cal]
175	            cal_ys = [y for _, y in all_cal]
176	            cal_w = max(cal_xs) + max(cal_xs) // 4
177	            cal_h = max(cal_ys) + max(cal_ys) // 4
178	
179	            if frame_w < cal_w or frame_h < cal_h:
180	                sx = frame_w / float(_CAL_W)
181	                sy = frame_h / float(_CAL_H)
182	                self._log(f"scaling coords for {frame_w}x{frame_h} by {sx:.3f}x{sy:.3f}")
183	                hold = {
184	                    ch: (int(self._cal_hold_pixels[ch][0] * sx),
185	                         int(self._cal_hold_pixels[ch][1] * sy))
186	                    for ch in CHANNELS
187	                }
188	                edge = {
189	                    ch: (int(self._cal_edge_pixels[ch][0] * sx),
190	                         int(self._cal_edge_pixels[ch][1] * sy))
191	                    for ch in CHANNELS
192	                }
193	            else:
194	                hold = dict(self._cal_hold_pixels)
195	                edge = dict(self._cal_edge_pixels)
196	            cached = (hold, edge)
197	            self._scaled_cache[key] = cached
198	            return cached
199	
200	    def _on_frame(self, frame: Frame) -> None:
201	        """Camera frame listener -- runs in the capture thread.
202	
203	        Prefers the full-resolution raw frame from the capture device when
204	        available, so detection is unaffected by the working/buffer downscale
205	        used for the live view.
206	
207	        After detection, attaches a per-frame snapshot to `frame.meta` so the
208	        view path can render scrub-accurate overlays from buffered frames.
209	        """
210	        img = frame.detect_image()
211	        if img is None:
212	            return
213	        h, w = img.shape[:2]
214	        hold_px, edge_px = self._scale_pixels(w, h)
215	        self._detect(img, hold_px, edge_px)
216	
217	        with self._lock:
218	            snap_state = dict(self._cached_result) if self._cached_result else {}
219	            snap_markers = {
220	                ch: {
221	                    "pressed": self._pressed[ch],
222	                    "hold_dist": self._hold_dist[ch],
223	                    "edge_dist": self._edge_dist[ch],
224	                    "edge_active": self._edge_active[ch],
225	                } for ch in CHANNELS
226	            }
227	            patch_r = self._patch_r
228	        if frame.meta is None:
229	            frame.meta = {}
230	        frame.meta["detect_video"] = {
231	            "state": snap_state,
232	            "markers": snap_markers,
233	            "patch_r": patch_r,
234	        }
235	
236	    def _sample_at(self, frame: np.ndarray, px: int, py: int) -> np.ndarray:
237	        """Average a small patch around (px, py)."""
238	        h, w = frame.shape[:2]
239	        px = max(0, min(px, w - 1))
240	        py = max(0, min(py, h - 1))
241	        r = self._patch_r
242	        y0, y1 = max(0, py - r), min(h, py + r + 1)
243	        x0, x1 = max(0, px - r), min(w, px + r + 1)
244	        patch = frame[y0:y1, x0:x1]
245	        if patch.size == 0:
246	            return np.zeros(3, dtype=np.float64)
247	        return patch.astype(np.float64).mean(axis=(0, 1))
248	
249	    @staticmethod
250	    def _brightness(color: np.ndarray) -> float:
251	        """Max channel value -- triggers on any color or white."""
252	        d = float(max(0.0, color[0], color[1], color[2]))
253	        return 0.0 if np.isnan(d) else d
254	
255	    def _color_signal(self, color: np.ndarray, ch: str) -> float:
256	        """Color-filtered signal -- only the button's own color triggers.
257	
258	        Scales by saturation ratio (max-min)/max so white/gray pixels
259	        produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance.
260	        """
261	        cmax = float(max(color[0], color[1], color[2]))
262	        if cmax < 1.0:
263	            return 0.0
264	        cmin = float(min(color[0], color[1], color[2]))
265	        sat_ratio = (cmax - cmin) / cmax
266	
267	        tw, rw = _COLOR_FILTER[ch]
268	        target = tw[0]*color[0] + tw[1]*color[1] + tw[2]*color[2]
269	        reject = max(0.0, rw[0]*color[0] + rw[1]*color[1] + rw[2]*color[2])
270	        d = float((target - reject) * sat_ratio)
271	        return 0.0 if np.isnan(d) else d
272	
273	    def _detect(
274	        self,
275	        frame: np.ndarray,
276	        hold_pixels: dict[str, tuple[int, int]],
277	        edge_pixels: dict[str, tuple[int, int]],
278	    ):
279	        """Run detection on a new camera frame. Called from capture thread."""
280	        result: dict[str, dict] = {}
281	        for ch in CHANNELS:
282	            hx, hy = hold_pixels[ch]
283	            ex, ey = edge_pixels[ch]
284	            hold_color = self._sample_at(frame, hx, hy)
285	            edge_color = self._sample_at(frame, ex, ey)
286	
287	            hold_dist = self._brightness(hold_color)
288	            edge_dist = self._color_signal(edge_color, ch)
289	
290	            with self._lock:
291	                self._hold_dist[ch] = hold_dist
292	                self._edge_dist[ch] = edge_dist
293	
294	                if not self._pressed[ch]:
295	                    if hold_dist > self._hold_thresh:
296	                        self._pressed[ch] = True
297	                else:
298	                    if hold_dist < self._hold_release:
299	                        self._pressed[ch] = False
300	
301	                edge_on = edge_dist > self._edge_thresh[ch]
302	                if edge_on and not self._edge_active[ch]:
303	                    self._press_count[ch] += 1
304	                self._edge_active[ch] = edge_on
305	
306	                result[ch] = {
307	                    "pressed": self._pressed[ch],
308	                    "baseline": min(4095, int(hold_dist * _DIST_SCALE)),
309	                    "edge_line": min(4095, int(edge_dist * _DIST_SCALE)),
310	                    "press_count": self._press_count[ch],
311	                }
312	
313	        with self._lock:
314	            self._cached_result = result
315	
316	    def update(self, sample: Sample) -> dict:
317	        """Return the latest detection result (computed in capture thread)."""
318	        with self._lock:
319	            cached = self._cached_result
320	
321	        if cached is not None:
322	            return cached
323	
324	        cam_status = self._cam.status()
325	        msg = "no_device" if not cam_status.get("active") else "waiting"
326	        return {ch: {
327	            "pressed": False, "baseline": 0, "edge_line": 0,
328	            "press_count": 0, "camera": msg,
329	        } for ch in CHANNELS}
330	
331	    # --- Chart schema -------------------------------------------------------
332	
333	    def chart_schema(self) -> list[dict]:
334	        """Per-fret hold + edge signals (no raw ADC)."""
335	        return [
336	            make_slot_schema(ch, [
337	                {"key": "baseline", "label": "Hold",
338	                 "color": CH_COLORS[ch], "width": 1.5},
339	                {"key": "edge_line", "label": "Edge",
340	                 "color": "#e94560", "width": 1.5, "dash": [2, 2]},
341	            ])
342	            for ch in CHANNELS
343	        ]
344	
345	    # --- Overlay extension --------------------------------------------------
346	
347	    def overlays(self) -> list[dict]:
348	        """Expose sensor markers as an overlay layer for the video viewport."""
349	        return [{"name": "detect_video.markers", "draw": self._draw_markers}]
350	
351	    def _draw_markers(self, image, frame: Optional[Frame] = None) -> None:
352	        h, w = image.shape[:2]
353	        hold_px, edge_px = self._scale_pixels(w, h)
354	
355	        # Prefer the per-frame snapshot when available (scrub fidelity); fall
356	        # back to live state for live frames or when the frame predates the
357	        # current detector instance.
358	        snap_meta = None
359	        if frame is not None and frame.meta:
360	            snap_meta = frame.meta.get("detect_video")
361	        if snap_meta is not None:
362	            markers = snap_meta.get("markers", {})
363	            patch_r = int(snap_meta.get("patch_r", self._patch_r))
364	            snap = {
365	                ch: (
366	                    hold_px[ch],
367	                    edge_px[ch],
368	                    bool(markers.get(ch, {}).get("pressed", False)),
369	                    float(markers.get(ch, {}).get("hold_dist", 0.0)),
370	                    float(markers.get(ch, {}).get("edge_dist", 0.0)),
371	                    bool(markers.get(ch, {}).get("edge_active", False)),
372	                ) for ch in CHANNELS
373	            }
374	        else:
375	            with self._lock:
376	                snap = {
377	                    ch: (
378	                        hold_px[ch],
379	                        edge_px[ch],
380	                        self._pressed[ch],
381	                        self._hold_dist[ch],
382	                        self._edge_dist[ch],
383	                        self._edge_active[ch],
384	                    ) for ch in CHANNELS
385	                }
386	                patch_r = self._patch_r
387	
388	        for ch, ((hx, hy), (ex, ey), pressed, hold_d, edge_d, edge_on) in snap.items():
389	            color = _MARKER_COLORS[ch]
390	            hold_ring = _PRESSED_COLOR if pressed else _IDLE_COLOR
391	
392	            cv2.rectangle(image, (hx - patch_r, hy - patch_r),
393	                          (hx + patch_r, hy + patch_r), color, 1)
394	            cv2.circle(image, (hx, hy), _MARKER_RADIUS, hold_ring, _MARKER_THICK)
395	
396	            cv2.line(image, (hx, hy), (ex, ey), color, 1)
397	            edge_ring = _PRESSED_COLOR if edge_on else _IDLE_COLOR
398	            cv2.rectangle(image, (ex - patch_r, ey - patch_r),
399	                          (ex + patch_r, ey + patch_r), color, 1)
400	            cv2.circle(image, (ex, ey), self._EDGE_RADIUS, edge_ring, self._EDGE_THICK)
401	
402	            label = f"{ch[0].upper()} h{hold_d:.0f} e{edge_d:.0f}"
403	            cv2.putText(image, label, (hx + _MARKER_RADIUS + 4, hy + 5),
404	                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, _FONT_SCALE, color, _FONT_THICK)

1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for the marvin firmware. Newest entries at the top.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Project north star
8	
9	Vision-based guitar-playing robot. The marvin firmware captures live HDMI video from a Nintendo Wii (Guitar Hero / Rock Band), runs vision on it, and drives actuators to fret and strum a real guitar.
10	
11	- **Target:** SAM9X75 Curiosity (MPLAB Harmony v5.6.4, SAM9X7 DFP 1.9.170, vision v3.2.1)
12	- **Video source:** Wii → ElectronWarp (component → HDMI, 480p60) → Waveshare HDMI-to-CSI-2 adapter (TC358743) → SAM9X75 MIPI CSI-2 RX → ISC → SDRAM
13	- **Display:** Legato GUI (already showing a basic screen as of commit `3bb441a`)
14	
15	---
16	
17	## Current focus
18	
19	**End-to-end pipeline working as of 2026-05-02: source → TC358743 → CSI-2 @ 972 Mbps/lane → SAM9X75 → ISC DMA → DDR (BGRX32) → XLCDC OVR1 → LVDSC → 10.1" 1280×800 LVDS panel.**
20	
21	> **Configuration references:**
22	> - [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) — HDMI → DDR capture stage (CSI2DC, ISC, register settings, datasheet citations).
23	> - [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) — DDR → LCD display stage (XLCDC OVR1 wiring, pillarbox, cache coherence).
24	
25	Phase 5b (byte-level content verification) ✅. Phase 6 MVP (captured video on the LCD) ✅, now displaying 480p sources pillarboxed/letterboxed and 720p sources letterbox-only on the 1280×800 panel. Phase 7a/c (480p via Pi and Wii) ✅. Next: Phase 8 (vision stage) — HEO scaling no longer needed for 720p since the bigger panel accommodates native, only relevant if 1080p sources come into scope.
26	
27	### Original focus (for context — this is done)
28	
29	**TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge driver** — first real driver work on marvin. The bridge is the gate between "we have hardware wired up" and "we have pixels in memory."
30	
31	### Hardware context
32	
33	- **Bridge board:** Waveshare HDMI to CSI-2 Adapter v1/v2 (2-lane CSI, 27 MHz on-board XTAL, expected I2C address `0x0F`).
34	- **Source chain:** Wii → ElectronWarp (https://electron-shepherd.com/collections/all/products/electronwarp) → HDMI 480p60 → Waveshare → CSI-2 → SAM9X75.
35	- **Marvin pre-existing scaffolding:**

37	  - CSI driver: `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi/` — configured for 2 data lanes (`CSI_NUM_LANES = CSI_DATA_LANES_2`, `configuration.h:167`)

57

69	
70	#### Phase 1 — I2C probe & chip ID ✅ COMPLETE (2026-05-01)
71	
72	Smallest code that proves I2C works and the chip is present.
73	
74	**Result:** DBGU reports `TC358743: present (chipid=0x0000)` on every boot — TC358743 is on the bus at `0x0f`, ACKs our transactions, accepts the software reset, and returns a clean CHIPID read. Full I2C path validated end-to-end: FLEXCOM6 → PA24/PA25 → J29 → 22→15 adapter → Waveshare → TC358743.
75	
76	**File layout (throwaway-friendly):**
77	
78	- `default/src/tc358743.h` — public API: `TC358743_Initialize(void)`, `TC358743_Tasks(void)`.
79	- `default/src/tc358743.c` — implementation.
80	
81	Kept flat in `default/src/` (not under a `drivers/` subfolder). Phase 3 is where we decide the permanent shape (sensor framework vs standalone).
82	
83	**Integration touchpoints in marvin's existing scaffold:**
84	
85	- `app.c:APP_Initialize()` → add `TC358743_Initialize();` after the initial state assignment.
86	- `app.c:APP_Tasks()` → add `TC358743_Tasks();` unconditionally at the top of the function (it has its own internal state machine, so the app's outer `APP_STATE_*` switch doesn't gate it).
87	- `app.h` → no changes needed for Phase 1.
88	- The FLEXCOM6 I2C driver is already brought up by `SYS_Initialize` (`initialization.c:360`, `sysObj.drvI2C0 = DRV_I2C_Initialize(...)`), so the TC358743 module only needs `DRV_I2C_Open(DRV_I2C_INDEX_0, DRV_IO_INTENT_EXCLUSIVE)`.
89	- `printf` is retargeted to DBGU via `default/src/config/default/stdio/xc32_monitor.c` — standard `printf("...")` works out of the box.
90	
91	**Internal state machine (inside `tc358743.c`):**
92	
93	| State | What it does | Next state on success |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| `INIT` | `DRV_I2C_Open`, register transfer-event callback, print banner | `SWRESET_ASSERT` |
96	| `SWRESET_ASSERT` | Queue write to `SYSCTL` with Sreset bit set (see wire-level table below) | `SWRESET_WAIT_ASSERT` |
97	| `SWRESET_WAIT_ASSERT` | Wait for completion callback, then start ≥1 ms delay | `SWRESET_RELEASE` |
98	| `SWRESET_RELEASE` | Queue write to `SYSCTL` clearing Sreset bit | `SWRESET_WAIT_RELEASE` |
99	| `SWRESET_WAIT_RELEASE` | Wait for completion callback, then start ≥1 ms delay | `READ_CHIPID` |
100	| `READ_CHIPID` | Queue `WriteReadTransferAdd` (reg addr write + 2-byte read at slave `0x0f`) | `REPORT` |
101	| `REPORT` | `printf` the result, evaluate pass condition, transition to `DONE` | `DONE` |
102	| `DONE` | Idle — no-op | `DONE` |
103	| `ERROR` | Printed in the callback; no retry in Phase 1 | `ERROR` |
104	
105	The transfer-event callback sets a flag + stashes the `DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_EVENT` result; `TC358743_Tasks()` polls that flag to advance state.
106	
107	**Wire-level transactions:**
108	
109	- **SYSCTL Sreset assert** — 4-byte I2C write to slave `0x0f`:
110	  - Bytes: `0x00 0x02 0x01 0x00` (register addr `0x0002` MSB-first, value `0x0001` little-endian — matches kernel driver's `i2c_wrreg`).
111	- **SYSCTL Sreset release** — 4-byte I2C write to slave `0x0f`:
112	  - Bytes: `0x00 0x02 0x00 0x00` (value `0x0000`).
113	- **CHIPID read** — 2-byte write then 2-byte read at slave `0x0f`:
114	  - Write phase: `0x00 0x00` (register addr `0x0000` MSB-first).
115	  - Read phase: 2 bytes, little-endian — stored as `rx[0]` = low byte (revision, `MASK_REVID = 0x00ff`), `rx[1]` = high byte (chip-id field, `MASK_CHIPID = 0xff00`).
116	
117	**Pass condition (matches kernel driver, `tc358743.c:2210-2215`):**
118	
119	- No I2C error on any of the three transactions.
120	- `rx[1]` (high byte of CHIPID) is `0x00`.
121	
122	If both hold, we print e.g. `"TC358743: present (chipid=0x%02X%02X)\n"` and advance to `DONE`. Otherwise we print the error and halt in `ERROR`.
123	
124	Note the kernel driver's weak identity check: upper byte must be zero, but the lower byte (revision) isn't constrained. Our probe follows the same convention — we don't hard-code an expected revision.
125	
126	**Delay strategy:**
127	
128	TC358743 datasheet requires ≥1 ms after Sreset before the next I2C transaction. Use Harmony's `SYS_TIME` service — it's already initialized in `SYS_Initialize` (`initialization.c:376`) and marvin's own ISC code uses it (`drv_isc.c:32-34`, `plib_isc.c:12-15`).
129	
130	Non-blocking pattern inside the state machine: the `SWRESET_WAIT_*` states call `SYS_TIME_DelayMS(1, &handle)` once (on entry) and then `SYS_TIME_DelayIsComplete(handle)` each tick until true, at which point the state advances. Avoids blocking `APP_Tasks()` (and Legato rendering with it) during the delay. The full init in Phase 3 will have many more delays, so the non-blocking shape earns its keep.
131	
132	**Buffers (static, module-scoped, lifetime spans the async transaction):**
133	
134	- `static uint8_t txBuf[4];`
135	- `static uint8_t rxBuf[2];`
136	- `static DRV_HANDLE i2cHandle;`
137	- `static volatile DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_EVENT lastEvt;` (written by the ISR-context callback; read by `_Tasks`)
138	- `static volatile bool evtReady;` (callback→Tasks handshake)
139	
140	**Error cases we expect to debug during bring-up:**
141	
142	- I2C NAK on the first SYSCTL write → wrong slave address (`0x0f` wrong — check A0 pin tie-off on Waveshare), or the cable/adapter is backwards, or PA24/PA25 aren't muxed to FLEXCOM6.
143	- `rxBuf = {0xff, 0xff}` → no ACK but our code didn't detect the NAK — would indicate a driver-level issue, not the chip.
144	- Nothing on DBGU at all → DBGU retarget path broken, or we're hanging in `DRV_I2C_Open`.
145	
146	**Exit criteria:**
147	
148	DBGU output contains `TC358743: present (chipid=0x...)` with the upper byte equal to `0x00`, after a power cycle of the board. No I2C errors printed.
149	
150	**Explicitly out of scope for Phase 1 (deferred to later phases):**
151	
152	- Hardware RESET via PC19 (see 2026-05-01 decision — software reset only).
153	- Retries, timeouts, or recovery from `ERROR`.
154	- Reading revision and printing the Toshiba datasheet name.
155	- Any HDMI / CSI register programming.
156	- Hooking into the `drv_image_sensor` framework.
157	
158	#### Phase 2 — Register access helpers ✅ CODE COMPLETE (2026-05-01, pending flash verify)
159	
160	TC358743 has 16-bit register addresses and mixed 8/16/32-bit data widths. Port the Linux driver's `i2c_wr*` + `i2c_rd*` family, one-for-one, against FLEXCOM6 TWI.
161	
162	**API (module-internal, `static` in `tc358743.c`):**
163	
164	```c
165	static bool tc358743_wr(uint16_t reg, const uint8_t *vals, size_t n);
166	static bool tc358743_rd(uint16_t reg, uint8_t *vals, size_t n);
167	static bool tc358743_wr8(uint16_t reg, uint8_t val);
168	static bool tc358743_wr16(uint16_t reg, uint16_t val);
169	static bool tc358743_wr32(uint16_t reg, uint32_t val);
170	static bool tc358743_rd8(uint16_t reg, uint8_t *val);
171	static bool tc358743_rd16(uint16_t reg, uint16_t *val);
172	static bool tc358743_rd32(uint16_t reg, uint32_t *val);
173	static bool tc358743_wr16_and_or(uint16_t reg, uint16_t mask, uint16_t val);
174	```
175	
176	All return `true` on success, `false` on any I2C error. Values are little-endian on the wire (matches kernel driver's `i2c_wrreg`/`i2c_rdreg` via `cpu_to_le32`/`le32_to_cpu`). Register addresses go out big-endian (MSB first) — also matches kernel driver.
177	
178	**Sync mechanism:**
179	
180	Each helper runs synchronously from the caller's view:
181	
182	1. Clear module-scoped `xferDone` / `xferErr` flags.
183	2. Issue `DRV_I2C_WriteTransferAdd` / `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransferAdd`.
184	3. Spin on `while (!xferDone && !xferErr)`.
185	4. Return success/failure.
186	
187	A single shared transfer-event callback flips the flags. FLEXCOM TWI is interrupt-driven on SAM9X7, so the spin loop doesn't need to pump anything — the ISR fires and the flag flips.
188	
189	**Blocking implications:**
190	
191	Each helper blocks for the duration of its I2C transaction (~100-500 µs at 400 kHz depending on size). Phase 3's init sequence may do 50+ transactions plus an EDID load; total boot-time block is expected to be tens of ms. Legato's initial animation may show a brief pause at startup. Acceptable — init runs once at boot.
192	
193	If any Phase 3+ use case needs to issue I2C without blocking (e.g. runtime format change), we add an async variant then. YAGNI for now.
194	
195	**Refactor of Phase 1:**
196	
197	Replace the ~10-state machine with imperative code in `TC358743_Initialize`:
198	
199	```c
200	open i2c
```

```text
1	# Fret-Tuner Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Web-based Python tool for developing and refining fret-press detection algorithms. Consumes the same raw ADC data the firmware sees -- either live from the board over UART or replayed from a captured CSV -- runs detection logic in Python, and visualizes everything in an interactive browser UI. Optionally sends actuation commands back to the microcontroller, moving the entire detection and strum-timing pipeline to the PC for rapid iteration.
6	
7	## Video reference (always-on)
8	
9	A first-class always-on subsystem. The UI exposes a video viewport at all times; behavior is independent of which detector is active.
10	
11	**Primary role**: time-aligned visual reference and recording against the ADC sample timeline and any derived signals (waveforms, detector state, fret/strum events). The question it answers: does what was on screen at time *t* match what the ADC and algorithms reported at *t*?
12	
13	**Secondary roles**: debugging alignment between capture and charts, reviewing a session after the fact, documenting false positives/negatives.
14	
15	### Requirements
16	
17	- **Primacy**: video reference is a first-class always-on subsystem, not gated on detector choice.
18	- **Source ownership**: the fret-tuner **backend** owns the camera. Exactly one source feeds the reference ring buffer at a time. The source is selectable in the UI from cameras enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option, plus any video file supplied for replay.
19	- **Buffer**: server-side ring buffer with **≥30 s wall-clock coverage** at a **target 30 Hz** capture rate. The buffer accepts whatever rate the camera delivers, sized to retain ≥30 s even when the source runs as fast as 60 Hz.
20	- **Synchronization**: every buffered frame carries a sample-clock timestamp anchored to the ADC stream so that any time *t* in the chart timeline maps to the closest buffered frame.
21	- **Live behavior**: while playing, the browser shows the most recent server frame with overlays composed for that frame's *t*.
22	- **Paused / scrubbing**: when paused, or while panning/zooming the charts, the video display follows the chart cursor / center time, picking the closest buffered frame.
23	- **Overlays**: per-frame composition (live and paused) at the display path's natural rate. Required minimum set:
24	    - 5 fret **pressed-state** indicators (per ADC channel)
25	    - **strum state** indicators (down + up, sourced from the actuator pipeline)
26	    - **scrub-time** text cursor
27	  Detectors may register additional overlay layers via the extension hook (see [Detection Algorithm Contract → Overlay extension](#overlay-extension)).
28	- **Detector consumption**: detectors that need pixel data (e.g. `detect_video`) **read from the reference buffer**; they do not own a separate camera grab.
29	
30	## Actuation (always-on)
31	
32	A first-class always-on subsystem that owns the GPIO command serial link to the actuator microcontroller. Behavior is independent of which detector is active and of where the ADC data comes from (live serial, CSV replay, or none).
33	
34	**Primary role**: consume detector state each tick, run the strum timing pipeline (chord window, FIFO scheduling, fret early/late, strum pulse), and emit a 1-byte GPIO bitmask to the actuator board over UART.
35	
36	### Requirements
37	
38	- **Primacy**: actuation is a first-class always-on subsystem, not a side effect of opening a data port. It can be enabled with any detector and any data source (including CSV-only replay against a live actuator board).
39	- **Source ownership**: the actuator owns its own `serial.Serial` handle. The port is selectable in the UI from ports enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option.
40	- **Port sharing**: the actuator port may name the same `/dev/cu.*` device as an ADC data port (single-board case). In that case the backend opens the device once and shares the handle between the data reader and the actuator writer; the writer never blocks on the reader and vice versa.
41	- **Reconnect**: when the actuator port is lost (unplug, USB sleep, etc.) the writer goes silent without raising; on reconnect, output resumes. Auto-reconnect runs at the same cadence as the data-port reconnect.
42	- **Enable gate**: a UI toggle gates output at the *bitmask* level. When disabled, the timing pipeline still runs (and reports `output_mask = 0`), but no bytes are written. Manual GPIO override (`manual_output`) still works when actuation is disabled, so individual buttons can be poked from the browser without engaging the full pipeline.
43	- **Always-on lifecycle**: created at server startup, persists across detector switches, never owned by a detector.
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	The backend is organized around two **always-on subsystems** (video reference, actuation) and one swappable **detector subsystem**. Always-on subsystems own their I/O and run regardless of which detector is active. The detector consumes whatever inputs it needs (ADC stream, video frames, etc.), produces detection state, and feeds it to the actuator.
48	
49	```
50	Browser (localhost:8080)
51	  ├── Video viewport (live or scrubbed frame + composited overlays)
52	  ├── uPlot charts (zoom, pan, pause)
53	  ├── Controls (camera source, actuator port, detector, params, recording)
54	  └── WebSocket  (sample data, detector state, sources, actuator status)
55	        ↕
56	FastAPI backend (Python)
57	  ├── camera.py          (OpenCV capture → shared ring buffer, ≥30 s @ ≥30 Hz)   [always-on]
58	  ├── actuator.py        (strum timing pipeline + GPIO serial TX)                 [always-on]
59	  ├── stream.py          (serial/CSV ADC source for ADC-based detectors)
60	  ├── detect_*.py        (consume samples and/or video frames; emit overlay layers)
61	  └── server.py          (WebSocket + HTTP video transport, subsystem wiring)
62	        ↕
63	Microcontrollers (PIC32CM)
64	  ├── Data board   →  fret_scan + data_stream     (12-byte ADC frames over UART)
65	  └── Actuator board → cmd_receive                (1-byte bitmask → GPIO assert/release)
66	                       The data board and actuator board may be the same physical
67	                       device sharing one UART, or two different devices.
68	```
69	
70	Browser and backend are deployed as a split / resizable layout: video viewport and ADC charts are co-equal, neither dominant by default. The shared video ring buffer lives in the backend; detector pixel consumers and the browser display both read from it.
71	
72	## File Layout
73	
74	```
75	tools/fret-tuner/
76	    fret-tuner.py          # CLI entry point (launches server, opens browser)
77	    server.py              # FastAPI app, WebSocket, data pipeline wiring
78	    camera.py              # OpenCV capture + shared video ring buffer
79	    index.html             # Browser UI (uPlot charts + video viewport, no build step)
80	    stream.py              # Serial + CSV data sources
81	    actuator.py            # Strum timing pipeline (port of fret_button.c)
82	    detect_threshold.py    # Detection: fixed per-channel hysteresis
83	    detect_trough.py       # Detection: baseline + trough FSM
84	    detect_slope.py        # Detection: EMA + slope FSM with re-press handling
85	    detect_video.py        # Detection: pixel sampling against the reference buffer
86	    video_calibrate.py     # Standalone helper for marking detect_video sensor coords
87	    requirements.txt       # Python dependencies
88	    SPEC.md                # This file
89	    .gitignore
90	
91	firmware/fretboard/
92	    cmd_receive.c          # UART RX command handler
93	    cmd_receive.h          # Header
94	```
95	
96	## Data Source
97	
98	### UART Binary Frame (micro → PC)
99	
100	The fretboard firmware streams 12-byte packed frames at **500 Hz** over SERCOM1 USART at **115200 baud** (8N1):
101	
102	```
103	Offset  Size   Field
104	------  -----  -----
105	0       1      Start byte (0x03)
106	1       2      Green   (uint16 LE, 12-bit ADC)
107	3       2      Red     (uint16 LE)
108	5       2      Yellow  (uint16 LE)
109	7       2      Blue    (uint16 LE)
110	9       2      Orange  (uint16 LE)
111	11      1      End byte (0xFC)
112	```
113	
114	### Command Byte (PC → micro)
115	
116	Single byte bitmask sent over the same serial connection (full-duplex). Each bit directly controls one GPIO output:
117	
118	```
119	Bit   Output
120	---   ------
121	0     Green fret
122	1     Red fret
123	2     Yellow fret
124	3     Blue fret
125	4     Orange fret
126	5     Strum down
127	6     Strum up
128	```
129	
130	Bit = 1 → assert (drive low). Bit = 0 → release (tri-state). The firmware applies the latest received byte each tick. When no bytes are received, outputs remain unchanged.
131	
132	### Serial Auto-Reconnect
133	
134	When the USB serial connection is lost (board unplugged, USB sleep, etc.), the feed loop catches the error, closes the stale serial handle, and retries opening the port every 2 seconds until the device reappears. On disconnect and reconnect, the server pushes `serial_status` messages over WebSocket so the browser UI can display the current state (amber "Serial disconnected -- reconnecting..." while down, green "Connected" on recovery). CSV replay sources are not affected.
135	
136	### CSV Replay Format
137	
138	CSV files captured from Microchip Data Visualizer. Expected columns:
139	
140	```
141	timestamp,BLUE RAW,BLUE,GREEN RAW,GREEN,ORANGE RAW,ORANGE,RED RAW,RED,YELLOW RAW,YELLOW
142	```
143	
144	Only the `timestamp` and `* RAW` columns are consumed.
145	
146	## Detection Algorithm Contract
147	
148	Each detector lives in its own `detect_*.py` file and exports a `Detector` class:
149	
150	```python
151	class Detector:
152	    @classmethod
153	    def default_params(cls) -> dict:
154	        """Return default parameter values."""
155	
156	    def __init__(self, **params):
157	        """Accept tunable parameters as keyword args."""
158	
159	    def update(self, sample: Sample) -> dict:
160	        """Process one sample. Return per-channel state dict:
161	        {
162	            "green":  {"pressed": bool, "baseline": int, ...},
163	            ...
164	        }
165	        """
166	```
167	
168	The `update()` return dict must include `"pressed"` (bool) and `"baseline"` (int) per channel. Additional keys are detector-specific and available for charting.
169	
170	The server auto-injects `"raw"` (the raw ADC reading for that channel) into each per-channel state dict before charting, so detectors do not need to copy it themselves.
171	
172	### Chart schema
173	
174	Detectors describe what their five chart slots should display via:
175	
176	```python
177	class Detector:
178	    def chart_schema(self) -> list[dict]:
179	        """Return 5 slot specs:
180	        {
181	            "id":      str,             # state-dict key (e.g. "green")
182	            "label":   str,             # axis label
183	            "color":   "#rrggbb",
184	            "y_range": [min, max],
185	            "series":  [
186	                {"key": str, "label": str, "color": "#rrggbb",
187	                 "width": float, "dash": [int, int] | None},
188	                ...
189	            ],
190	        }
191	        """
192	```
193	
194	Each `series.key` names a field inside that channel's state dict. `stream.adc_chart_schema(extra_series=[...])` builds the conventional `raw + <extras>` layout for ADC detectors. Detectors with no use for raw ADC (e.g. `detect_video`) simply omit the `"raw"` series.
195	
196	The browser rebuilds its chart slots whenever a new schema arrives, so switching detectors swaps the chart contents (labels, colors, y-range, plotted series) along with the algorithm.
197	
198	### Overlay extension
199	
200	Detectors may optionally contribute named overlay layers to the video viewport:
201	
202	```python
203	class Detector:
204	    def overlays(self) -> list[OverlayLayer]:
205	        """Optional. Return list of overlay layers to draw on the video.
206	        Each layer = {name: str, draw(ctx, frame_meta, sample_state) -> None}.
207	        Returning [] (or omitting the method) means no detector-specific overlays.
208	        """
209	        return []
210	```
211	
212	Layers compose on top of the always-on minimum set (fret pressed-state, strum state, scrub time). Transport for overlay drawcalls is implementation-defined: the server may bake them into delivered frames, or stream drawcall metadata (see [WebSocket Protocol](#websocket-protocol) `video_meta`) for client-side compositing.
213	
214	`detect_video`, for example, registers a layer that draws its sensor sample points and per-button signal levels.
215	
216	### Adding a new detector
217	
218	1. Create `tools/fret-tuner/detect_myalgo.py`
219	2. Implement a `Detector` class following the contract above
220	3. Select it from the dropdown in the browser UI (or `--detector detect_myalgo` on the CLI)
221	
222	The server hot-reloads detector modules on switch, so you can edit the file and switch to it without restarting.
223	
224	## Bundled Detector: detect_threshold
225	
226	Fixed per-channel hysteresis. Matches the current firmware `fret_detect.c`.
227	
228	| Parameter | Default | Description |
229	|-----------|---------|-------------|
230	| `GREEN_PRESS` | 2500 | Green press threshold |
231	| `GREEN_RELEASE` | 2800 | Green release threshold |
232	| `RED_PRESS` | 2500 | Red press threshold |
233	| `RED_RELEASE` | 2800 | Red release threshold |
234	| `YELLOW_PRESS` | 1500 | Yellow press threshold |
235	| `YELLOW_RELEASE` | 1700 | Yellow release threshold |
236	| `BLUE_PRESS` | 1500 | Blue press threshold |
237	| `BLUE_RELEASE` | 1700 | Blue release threshold |
238	| `ORANGE_PRESS` | 2000 | Orange press threshold |
239	| `ORANGE_RELEASE` | 2200 | Orange release threshold |
240	
241	## Bundled Detector: detect_trough
242	
243	Baseline + trough FSM. Three states: IDLE → DESCENDING → PRESSED.
244	
245	| Parameter | Default | Description |
246	|-----------|---------|-------------|
247	| `MIN_DROP` | 200 | ADC counts below baseline to begin descent tracking |
248	| `RISE_CONFIRM` | 50 | ADC counts above running minimum to confirm press |
249	| `RELEASE_MARGIN` | 300 | Counts within baseline to trigger release |
250	| `BASELINE_DECAY_RATE` | 250 | Samples between 1-count baseline decrements |
251	
252	## Actuator (actuator.py)
253	
254	Python port of `firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c`. Translates detector press/release edges into a timed sequence of fret assertions and strum pulses.
255	
256	### Timing Pipeline
257	
258	1. **Chord window** -- new presses within `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` are accumulated
259	2. **Chord commit** -- schedules note assert at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS - FRET_EARLY_MS` and strum at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`
260	3. **Note FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending fret assertions, processed in order
261	4. **Strum FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending strum triggers, alternating up/down
262	5. **Strum pulse** -- held for `STRUM_PULSE_MS`, then released
263	6. **Delayed releases** -- each released fret is scheduled for release at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`, skipped if still needed by pending notes/strums
264	
265	### Timing Parameters
266	
267	| Parameter | Default | Description |
268	|-----------|---------|-------------|
269	| `STRUM_DELAY_MS` | 220 | Delay from chord commit to strum |
270	| `FRET_EARLY_MS` | 50 | How early frets assert before strum |
271	| `STRUM_PULSE_MS` | 50 | How long the strum output is held |
272	| `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` | 20 | Window for accumulating chord presses |
273	
274	All timing is driven by sample timestamps, not wall clock, so the pipeline behaves identically in live and CSV replay modes.
275	
276	### Output
277	
278	Computes a 7-bit bitmask each tick and writes it to the serial port. Actuation is disabled by default and toggled from the browser UI.
279	
280	## Firmware: cmd_receive
281	
282	Minimal command receiver added to the fretboard firmware. Replaces `fret_detect` and `fret_button` in `main.c` -- the microcontroller becomes a scan/stream/actuate relay.
283	
284	### Main loop (modified)
285	
286	```c
287	fret_scan_all();
288	data_stream_send();
289	cmd_receive_update();
290	```
291	
292	### cmd_receive_update()
293	
294	1. Checks `SERCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` for available bytes
295	2. Reads all available bytes, keeps the last one
296	3. Applies the bitmask: for each bit, asserts (drive low + output enable) or releases (input enable) the corresponding GPIO
297	
298	## Browser UI
299	
300	Single-file HTML served by the backend at `http://localhost:8080`. Loads uPlot from CDN (no build step).
301	
302	### Charts
303	
304	- 5 stacked uPlot time-series charts, one per fret slot (green, red, yellow, blue, orange)
305	- The active detector's `chart_schema()` defines the series, labels, colors, and y-range for each slot. ADC detectors plot raw ADC + their baseline / threshold lines; `detect_video` plots its hold + edge signals (no raw ADC). Switching detectors swaps the chart contents.
306	- Shaded press bands and (where the detector emits `press_count`) re-press tick marks are overlaid in the slot color
307	- Native mouse-drag zoom, scroll-wheel zoom, double-click to reset
308	
309	### Controls (sidebar)
310	
311	- **Pause / Resume** -- freezes chart updates; data continues to buffer server-side
312	- **Window width** -- slider controlling visible time range (0.5--30 seconds)
313	- **Detector dropdown** -- switch between available `detect_*.py` modules live
314	- **Parameter sliders** -- dynamically generated from the active detector's `default_params()`, changes take effect immediately
315	- **Camera source dropdown** -- enumerated cameras + "none"; controls the always-on video reference
316	- **Actuator port dropdown** -- enumerated `/dev/cu.*` (or platform equivalent) serial ports + "none"; controls the always-on actuator. Selecting the same device as a live ADC data port shares the handle.
317	- **Actuation toggle** -- enable/disable writing command bytes (the timing pipeline runs either way)
318	- **Timing sliders** -- strum delay, fret early, strum pulse, chord window
319	- **Connection status** indicators -- separate badges for the data port and the actuator port
320	
321	### Layout
322	
323	Split / resizable two-pane layout. The **video viewport** and the **ADC charts** are co-equal first-class panes; neither is dominant by default and the user can resize the split. Sidebar controls remain to one side.
324	
325	### Video viewport
326	
327	Backed by the always-on subsystem in [Video reference (always-on)](#video-reference-always-on). UI surface:
328	
329	- **Source selector** -- lists cameras enumerated by the backend, plus "none" and any `--video FILE` replay file. Selection persisted by the backend, applied immediately.
330	- **Recording controls** -- start / stop / save buffer (writes paired video + ADC log; see [Recording & paired CSV replay](#recording--paired-csv-replay)). Default off.
331	- **Pause / scrub** -- synchronized with the charts' pause; chart center time drives the displayed frame.
332	- **Overlays** -- always-on minimum (5 fret pressed-state indicators, strum state, scrub time) plus any layers the active detector registers via [Overlay extension](#overlay-extension).
333	
334	### Recording & paired CSV replay
335	
336	- A live session can be **recorded**: the backend drains the reference ring buffer to a video file alongside the ADC sample log (CSV), with a shared time anchor written into the recording so the two replay in sync.
337	- `python fret-tuner.py --csv FILE [--video FILE]` replays both. If `--video` is omitted, the video viewport shows "no recorded video for this CSV" and disables source selection for the duration of the replay.
338	- Recording is started/stopped explicitly from the sidebar; default off.
339	
340	### WebSocket Protocol
341	
342	Sample data, detector state, and overlay metadata flow over the WebSocket; raw video frames are delivered over a parallel HTTP video transport (implementation choice; the existing tool uses MJPEG). Both share the same sample-clock timestamps so chart and video scrubbing target the same *t*.
343	
344	#### Master clock: the displayed video frame
345	
346	The currently displayed video frame is the single source of truth for *now*. Each captured frame has a `seq` (monotonic id) and a `t` (sample-clock timestamp), and every UI element (chart cursor, viewport scroll, overlay text) aligns to the *currently displayed* frame's `t` -- not to the latest ADC sample, the wall clock, or the network arrival time.
347	
348	- **Live mode**: the server emits a `frame_tick` message on every buffer write (~30 Hz). The browser updates `currentFrame = {seq, t}` and re-clips the chart's leading edge to that `t`. ADC samples that arrived *after* the latest displayed frame are buffered but not yet visible; they are revealed on the next tick. Chart movement is therefore quantized at the camera frame rate, which is the trade-off we accept to keep video, charts, and overlays exactly aligned.
349	- **Pause / scrub**: `frame_tick` is ignored. The user moves `currentFrame` via the timeline, frame-step buttons, or slow-mo playback. Each scrub action returns from the server with a `{seq, t}` pair, which the browser writes back into `currentFrame`.
350	- **CSV / no-camera fallback**: when no camera is attached, no `frame_tick` is emitted. The browser falls back to the latest ingested ADC sample timestamp as `currentFrame.t`, with `seq=null`.
351	
352	Server → client:
353	
354	```json
355	{"type": "data", "samples": [...], "state": [...], "actuator_mask": 0}
356	{"type": "frame_tick", "seq": 1234, "t": 12.345}          // ~30 Hz, camera only
357	{"type": "detector", "name": "...", "params": {...}, "available": [...],
358	 "timing": {...}, "actuate_enabled": false}
359	{"type": "serial_status", "connected": true}              // data port
360	{"type": "actuator_status", "connected": true,
361	 "available": [...], "active": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}   // actuator port
362	{"type": "video_meta", "t": 12.345, "layers": [...]}
363	{"type": "sources", "available": [...], "active": "..."}  // camera sources
364	{"type": "recording", "active": false, "path": null}
365	```
366	
367	Client → server:
368	
369	```json
370	{"type": "pause"}
371	{"type": "resume"}
372	{"type": "set_params", "params": {"KEY": value}}
373	{"type": "set_detector", "name": "detect_trough"}
374	{"type": "set_timing", "params": {"STRUM_DELAY_MS": 200}}
375	{"type": "set_actuate", "enabled": true}
376	{"type": "set_source", "name": "..."}            // camera source
377	{"type": "set_actuator_port", "name": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}  // or "none"
378	{"type": "manual_output", "mask": 0}
379	{"type": "record_start"}
380	{"type": "record_stop"}
381	```
382	
383	The backend also exposes:
384	
385	- `GET /api/sources` -- camera sources (mirror of the WS `sources` message)
386	- `GET /api/serial-ports` -- enumerated serial ports for the actuator dropdown
387	- `GET /video` -- live MJPEG of the working-resolution buffer (server-rendered overlays applied)
388	- `GET /video/snap?t=<sec>` -- single JPEG of the buffered frame closest to *t*. Response carries `X-Frame-Seq` and `X-Frame-Time` headers (and a matching `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`) so the browser can sync `currentFrame` to the snapped frame even when the snapped *t* differs from the requested *t*.
389	- `GET /video/step?dir=next|prev&n=N&{seq=S | t=T}` -- walk the ring buffer to the n-th next/prev frame. Address by `seq` for exact stepping (preferred when the browser holds a known frame); fall back to `t` for the first scrub when seq is unknown. Returns `{"seq": int, "t": float, "buffered": int}`.
390	
391	## CLI Reference
392	
393	```
394	usage: fret-tuner.py [-h] (--port PORT | --csv FILE) [--video FILE]
395	                     [--actuator-port PORT] [--camera ID]
396	                     [--detector MODULE] [--param KEY=VALUE] [--fast]
397	                     [--host HOST] [--web-port PORT]
398	```
399	
400	`--port` selects the **data** serial port (ADC frame source). `--actuator-port` selects the **actuator** serial port; if omitted, the actuator starts idle and a port can be chosen at runtime from the sidebar dropdown. If `--actuator-port` names the same device as `--port`, the backend opens it once and shares the handle for read and write.
401	
402	### Examples
403	
404	```bash
405	# Single board: ADC stream + actuator on the same port (handle is shared)
406	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
407	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202
408	
409	# Two boards: ADC stream on one device, actuator on another
410	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
411	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
412	
413	# CSV replay against a live actuator board
414	python fret-tuner.py --csv session.csv --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
415	
416	# CSV replay, no actuator (UI dropdown can attach one later)
417	python fret-tuner.py --csv ../../firmware/fretboard/fretboard-sample-raw.csv
418	
419	# Start with trough detector and custom parameters
420	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 --detector detect_trough \
421	    --param MIN_DROP=150 --param RISE_CONFIRM=30
422	
423	# Fast CSV replay (no real-time pacing)
424	python fret-tuner.py --csv capture.csv --fast
425	```
426	
427	## Dependencies
428	
429	Uses the repo-level `.venv` (Python 3.12). Required packages:
430	
431	- `pyserial >= 3.5`
432	- `numpy >= 1.24`
433	- `fastapi >= 0.115`
434	- `uvicorn[standard] >= 0.30`
435	- `websockets >= 12.0`
436	- `opencv-python` (server-side video capture and `detect_video`)
437	
438	## Bundled Detector: detect_video
439	
440	Pixel-sampling detector that **consumes the shared reference video buffer**. It does not own a camera and does not serve its own video stream; sensor sample points and per-button signal levels are exposed as an [overlay layer](#overlay-extension) for the viewport.
441	
442	Two sensor points per button, both above the strike line:
443	
444	- **Sensor 1 (hold)** -- brightness detect (color OR white). Sets `pressed=True` whenever max channel brightness exceeds `THRESHOLD`.
445	- **Sensor 2 (edge)** -- color-filtered leading-edge detect. Increments `press_count` on each new note arrival for strum timing.
446	
447	Detection thresholds are applied directly to raw pixel values (dark background is implicit zero, no settle/calibration phase).
448	
449	### Observed Game Colors (camera-captured BGR)
450	
451	Colors are highly saturated with negligible off-channel values:
452	
453	| Color  | B    | G    | R    | Notes |
454	|--------|------|------|------|-------|
455	| Red    | <10  | <10  | >100 | Almost completely red |
456	| Green  | <10  | >100 | <10  | Completely green |
457	| Blue   | >100 | ~67  | <10  | B dominant, G about 2/3 of B, low R |
458	| Yellow | <10  | ~100 | ~100 | Even mix of G and R, very low B |
459	| Orange | <10  | ~50  | >100 | R dominant, G about half of R, low B |
460	| White (fret bar) | ~160 | ~160 | ~160 | Equal channels at brightest, sat near 0 |
461	
462	The edge detector uses a color filter with saturation scaling `(max-min)/max` to reject white/gray fret bars regardless of camera white balance.
463	
464	### Parameters
465	
466	| Parameter | Default | Description |
467	|-----------|---------|-------------|
468	| `THRESHOLD` | 50 | Detection threshold (brightness for hold, color signal for edge) |
469	| `RELEASE_FRAC` | 60 | Release threshold as % of press threshold (hysteresis) |
470	| `PATCH_RADIUS` | 2 | Pixel averaging radius around sample point |
471	| `{COLOR}_X/Y` | varies | Hold sensor pixel coordinates per button |
472	| `{COLOR}_EX/EY` | varies | Edge sensor pixel coordinates per button |
473	
474	Camera selection lives in the always-on video subsystem, not the detector; there is no `DEVICE_ID` parameter here. Sensor markers are drawn through the `overlays()` hook, replacing the previous `SHOW_PREVIEW`/`/video` path.
475	
476	### Calibration
477	
478	Use `video_calibrate.py` to interactively mark sensor positions:
479	
480	```bash
481	# Full calibration (10 points: 5 hold + 5 edge)
482	python video_calibrate.py --device 0
483	
484	# Color sampling mode (inspect BGR values without calibrating)
485	python video_calibrate.py --sample
486	```
487	
488	## Future Work

The runtime UI would then expose a per-detector source picker. (Chart schemas already follow this model: each detector returns a `chart_schema()` and the browser rebuilds the 5 chart slots from it.) The current scope keeps `--port` / `--csv` as a top-level concern.
491	- Multi-detector overlay (compare two algorithms side-by-side on the same chart)
492	- Per-channel enable/disable toggles for actuation
493	- Latency measurement display (round-trip time from ADC sample to GPIO assertion)
494	- Multi-camera reference (more than one source recorded and replayable in sync)

2	Actuator -- Python port of firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c
3	
4	Translates detector press/release edges into a timed sequence of
5	fret assertions and strum pulses, then sends a 1-byte GPIO bitmask
6	to the actuator microcontroller over its own UART.
7	
8	Driven by sample timestamps (not wall clock) so behavior is identical
9	in live and CSV replay modes.
10	
11	The actuator is an always-on subsystem: it owns its own serial port
12	(or shares one with the data source when the same physical device
13	is used for both ADC streaming and GPIO output). Port selection,
14	reconnect, and enable-gating are managed here so the timing pipeline
15	runs regardless of which detector is active.

18	import logging
19	import threading
20	import time
21	from collections import deque
22	from typing import Callable, Optional
23	
24	import serial

26	from stream import CHANNELS

28	log = logging.getLogger("fret-tuner.actuator")

30	# Bitmask bit positions (must match cmd_receive.h)
31	BIT_GREEN = 1 << 0
32	BIT_RED = 1 << 1
33	BIT_YELLOW = 1 << 2
34	BIT_BLUE = 1 << 3
35	BIT_ORANGE = 1 << 4
36	BIT_STRUM_DOWN = 1 << 5
37	BIT_STRUM_UP = 1 << 6
38	
39	CHANNEL_BITS = {
40	    "green": BIT_GREEN,
41	    "red": BIT_RED,
42	    "yellow": BIT_YELLOW,
43	    "blue": BIT_BLUE,
44	    "orange": BIT_ORANGE,
45	}
46	
47	FIFO_CAP = 16
48	
49	DEFAULT_TIMING = {
50	    "STRUM_DELAY_MS": 220,
51	    "FRET_EARLY_MS": 50,
52	    "STRUM_PULSE_MS": 50,
53	    "CHORD_WINDOW_MS": 20,

55	
56	ACTUATOR_BAUDRATE = 115200
57	RECONNECT_INTERVAL = 2.0

59	
60	class _PendingNote:
61	    __slots__ = ("fret_mask", "assert_at")
62	
63	    def __init__(self, fret_mask: int, assert_at: float):
64	        self.fret_mask = fret_mask
65	        self.assert_at = assert_at
66	
67	
68	class _PendingStrum:
69	    __slots__ = ("fret_mask", "strum_at")
70	
71	    def __init__(self, fret_mask: int, strum_at: float):
72	        self.fret_mask = fret_mask
73	        self.strum_at = strum_at

75	
76	class Actuator:
77	    """Strum timing pipeline + always-on serial GPIO output.
78	
79	    Two attach modes:
80	
81	    * **owned**: actuator opens the port itself and manages reconnect.
82	      Use `attach(port_name)` / `detach()`.
83	    * **shared**: a serial handle was opened elsewhere (the data-side
84	      reader) and we just write to it. The owner is responsible for
85	      reopening on disconnect; after each reopen they re-call
86	      `attach_shared(...)` with the new handle.
87	    """
88	
89	    def __init__(self):
90	        self._ser: Optional[serial.Serial] = None
91	        self._port_name: Optional[str] = None
92	        self._owned: bool = False
93	        self._connected: bool = False
94	        self._enabled: bool = False
95	
96	        self.strum_delay_ms: float = DEFAULT_TIMING["STRUM_DELAY_MS"]
97	        self.fret_early_ms: float = DEFAULT_TIMING["FRET_EARLY_MS"]
98	        self.strum_pulse_ms: float = DEFAULT_TIMING["STRUM_PULSE_MS"]
99	        self.chord_window_ms: float = DEFAULT_TIMING["CHORD_WINDOW_MS"]
100	
101	        self._note_q: deque[_PendingNote] = deque(maxlen=FIFO_CAP)
102	        self._strum_q: deque[_PendingStrum] = deque(maxlen=FIFO_CAP)
103	
104	        self._release_at: dict[str, float] = {}
105	        self._release_pending: dict[str, bool] = {ch: False for ch in CHANNELS}
106	
107	        self._chord_open = False
108	        self._chord_start: float = 0.0
109	        self._chord_mask: int = 0
110	
111	        self._frets_active: int = 0
112	        self._strum_active = False
113	        self._strum_release_at: float = 0.0
114	        self._strum_direction = False
115	
116	        self._prev_pressed: dict[str, bool] = {ch: False for ch in CHANNELS}
117	        self._prev_press_count: dict[str, int] = {ch: 0 for ch in CHANNELS}
118	        self._output_mask: int = 0
119	
120	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
121	        self._listeners: list[Callable[[dict], None]] = []
122	        self._reconnect_stop = threading.Event()
123	        self._reconnect_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None
124	
125	    # ----- public introspection / config ---------------------------------
126	
127	    @property
128	    def enabled(self) -> bool:
129	        return self._enabled
130	
131	    @property
132	    def output_mask(self) -> int:
133	        return self._output_mask
134	
135	    def status(self) -> dict:
136	        return {
137	            "active": self._port_name is not None,
138	            "port": self._port_name,
139	            "owned": self._owned,
140	            "connected": self._connected,
141	            "enabled": self._enabled,
142	        }
143	
144	    def add_status_listener(self, fn: Callable[[dict], None]) -> None:
145	        self._listeners.append(fn)
146	
147	    def set_enabled(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
148	        self._enabled = enabled
149	        if not enabled:
150	            self._release_all()
151	        self._notify()
152	
153	    def set_timing(self, **params) -> None:
154	        for key, val in params.items():
155	            if key == "STRUM_DELAY_MS":
156	                self.strum_delay_ms = float(val)
157	            elif key == "FRET_EARLY_MS":
158	                self.fret_early_ms = float(val)
159	            elif key == "STRUM_PULSE_MS":
160	                self.strum_pulse_ms = float(val)
161	            elif key == "CHORD_WINDOW_MS":
162	                self.chord_window_ms = float(val)
163	
164	    # ----- port lifecycle ------------------------------------------------
165	
166	    def attach(self, port_name: str) -> bool:
167	        """Open `port_name` ourselves; the actuator owns the handle."""
168	        self.detach()
169	        try:
170	            ser = serial.Serial(
171	                port=port_name,
172	                baudrate=ACTUATOR_BAUDRATE,
173	                bytesize=serial.EIGHTBITS,
174	                parity=serial.PARITY_NONE,
175	                stopbits=serial.STOPBITS_ONE,
176	                timeout=0.1,
177	            )
178	        except (serial.SerialException, OSError) as exc:
179	            log.warning("actuator: open %s failed: %s", port_name, exc)
180	            with self._lock:
181	                self._port_name = port_name
182	                self._owned = True
183	                self._connected = False
184	                self._ser = None
185	            self._notify()
186	            self._start_reconnect_worker()
187	            return False
188	
189	        with self._lock:
190	            self._ser = ser
191	            self._port_name = port_name
192	            self._owned = True
193	            self._connected = True
194	        log.info("actuator: opened %s", port_name)
195	        self._notify()
196	        self._start_reconnect_worker()
197	        return True
198	
199	    def attach_shared(self, port_name: str, ser: serial.Serial) -> None:
200	        """Use an externally-owned handle. Caller manages connect/reconnect."""
201	        self.detach()
202	        with self._lock:
203	            self._ser = ser
204	            self._port_name = port_name
205	            self._owned = False
206	            self._connected = bool(ser and ser.is_open)
207	        log.info("actuator: attached shared port %s", port_name)
208	        self._notify()
209	
210	    def detach(self) -> None:
211	        """Release any current port (closes only if we own the handle)."""
212	        self._stop_reconnect_worker()
213	        with self._lock:
214	            ser = self._ser
215	            owned = self._owned
216	            self._ser = None
217	            self._port_name = None
218	            self._owned = False
219	            self._connected = False
220	        if owned and ser is not None:
221	            try:
222	                ser.close()
223	            except Exception:
224	                pass
225	        self._notify()
226	
227	    def is_using_port(self, port_name: str) -> bool:
228	        with self._lock:
229	            return self._port_name == port_name
230	
231	    # ----- timing pipeline -----------------------------------------------
232	
233	    def update(self, now_ms: float, detect_state: dict) -> int:
234	        """Process one tick. Returns the 7-bit output bitmask."""
235	        if not self._enabled:
236	            self._output_mask = 0
237	            return 0
238	
239	        presses = 0
240	        releases = 0
241	        for ch in CHANNELS:
242	            ch_state = detect_state.get(ch, {})
243	            pressed = ch_state.get("pressed", False)
244	            was_pressed = self._prev_pressed[ch]
245	
246	            press_count = ch_state.get("press_count")
247	            if press_count is not None:
248	                if press_count != self._prev_press_count[ch]:
249	                    presses |= CHANNEL_BITS[ch]
250	                self._prev_press_count[ch] = press_count
251	            else:
252	                if pressed and not was_pressed:
253	                    presses |= CHANNEL_BITS[ch]
254	
255	            if not pressed and was_pressed:
256	                releases |= CHANNEL_BITS[ch]
257	
258	            self._prev_pressed[ch] = pressed
259	
260	        if presses:
261	            if not self._chord_open:
262	                self._chord_open = True
263	                self._chord_start = now_ms
264	                self._chord_mask = 0
265	            self._chord_mask |= presses
266	
267	        for ch in CHANNELS:
268	            bit = CHANNEL_BITS[ch]
269	            if releases & bit:
270	                self._release_at[ch] = now_ms + self.strum_delay_ms
271	                self._release_pending[ch] = True
272	
273	        if self._chord_open and (now_ms - self._chord_start) >= self.chord_window_ms:
274	            self._chord_commit(now_ms)
275	
276	        if self._strum_active and now_ms >= self._strum_release_at:
277	            self._strum_active = False
278	
279	        self._process_notes(now_ms)
280	        self._process_strums(now_ms)
281	        self._process_releases(now_ms, detect_state)
282	
283	        mask = self._frets_active
284	        if self._strum_active:
285	            if self._strum_direction:
286	                mask |= BIT_STRUM_UP
287	            else:
288	                mask |= BIT_STRUM_DOWN
289	
290	        self._output_mask = mask
291	        self._send(mask)
292	        return mask
293	
294	    def write_manual(self, mask: int) -> bool:
295	        """Push a raw bitmask out the actuator port (used by the manual buttons).
296	
297	        Returns False if no port is attached or the write failed.
298	        Does not touch the timing pipeline or the enable gate.
299	        """
300	        return self._send(int(mask) & 0x7F)
301	
302	    def _chord_commit(self, now_ms: float) -> None:
303	        if len(self._note_q) >= FIFO_CAP or len(self._strum_q) >= FIFO_CAP:
304	            self._chord_open = False
305	            self._chord_mask = 0
306	            return
307	
308	        assert_at = now_ms + self.strum_delay_ms - self.fret_early_ms
309	        strum_at = now_ms + self.strum_delay_ms
310	
311	        if self._strum_q:
312	            last = self._strum_q[-1]
313	            earliest = last.strum_at + self.strum_pulse_ms
314	            if assert_at < earliest:
315	                assert_at = earliest
316	                strum_at = assert_at + self.fret_early_ms
317	
318	        self._note_q.append(_PendingNote(self._chord_mask, assert_at))
319	        self._strum_q.append(_PendingStrum(self._chord_mask, strum_at))
320	
321	        self._chord_open = False
322	        self._chord_mask = 0
323	
324	    def _process_notes(self, now_ms: float) -> None:
325	        while self._note_q:
326	            n = self._note_q[0]
327	            if now_ms < n.assert_at:
328	                break
329	
330	            for ch in CHANNELS:
331	                bit = CHANNEL_BITS[ch]
332	                need = bool(n.fret_mask & bit)
333	                have = bool(self._frets_active & bit)
334	                if need and not have:
335	                    self._frets_active |= bit
336	                elif not need and have:
337	                    self._frets_active &= ~bit
338	
339	            self._note_q.popleft()
340	
341	    def _process_strums(self, now_ms: float) -> None:
342	        while self._strum_q:
343	            s = self._strum_q[0]
344	            if now_ms < s.strum_at:
345	                break
346	
347	            self._strum_active = True
348	            self._strum_direction = not self._strum_direction
349	            self._strum_release_at = now_ms + self.strum_pulse_ms
350	
351	            self._strum_q.popleft()
352	
353	    def _process_releases(self, now_ms: float, detect_state: dict) -> None:
354	        for ch in CHANNELS:
355	            if not self._release_pending[ch]:
356	                continue
357	            if now_ms < self._release_at.get(ch, float("inf")):
358	                continue
359	
360	            ch_state = detect_state.get(ch, {})
361	            if ch_state.get("pressed", False):
362	                continue
363	
364	            bit = CHANNEL_BITS[ch]
365	            needed = False
366	            for n in self._note_q:
367	                if n.fret_mask & bit:
368	                    needed = True
369	                    break
370	            if not needed:
371	                for s in self._strum_q:
372	                    if s.fret_mask & bit:
373	                        needed = True
374	                        break
375	            if needed:
376	                continue
377	
378	            self._frets_active &= ~bit
379	            self._release_pending[ch] = False
380	
381	    def _release_all(self) -> None:
382	        self._frets_active = 0
383	        self._strum_active = False
384	        self._note_q.clear()
385	        self._strum_q.clear()
386	        self._chord_open = False
387	        self._chord_mask = 0
388	        for ch in CHANNELS:
389	            self._release_pending[ch] = False
390	        self._output_mask = 0
391	        self._send(0)
392	
393	    # ----- serial output -------------------------------------------------
394	
395	    def _send(self, mask: int) -> bool:
396	        with self._lock:
397	            ser = self._ser
398	            connected = self._connected
399	        if ser is None or not connected:
400	            return False
401	        if not ser.is_open:
402	            self._mark_disconnected()
403	            return False
404	        try:
405	            ser.write(bytes([mask & 0x7F]))
406	            return True
407	        except (serial.SerialException, OSError) as exc:
408	            log.warning("actuator: write failed: %s", exc)
409	            self._mark_disconnected()
410	            return False
411	
412	    def _mark_disconnected(self) -> None:
413	        owned = False
414	        ser_to_close = None
415	        with self._lock:
416	            if self._connected:
417	                self._connected = False
418	                if self._owned:
419	                    owned = True
420	                    ser_to_close = self._ser
421	                    self._ser = None
422	        if owned and ser_to_close is not None:
423	            try:
424	                ser_to_close.close()
425	            except Exception:
426	                pass
427	        self._notify()
428	
429	    # ----- reconnect (only for owned ports) ------------------------------
430	
431	    def _start_reconnect_worker(self) -> None:
432	        if self._reconnect_thread and self._reconnect_thread.is_alive():
433	            return
434	        self._reconnect_stop.clear()
435	        t = threading.Thread(
436	            target=self._reconnect_loop, name="actuator-reconnect", daemon=True,
437	        )
438	        self._reconnect_thread = t
439	        t.start()
440	
441	    def _stop_reconnect_worker(self) -> None:
442	        self._reconnect_stop.set()
443	        t = self._reconnect_thread
444	        if t is not None and t.is_alive():
445	            t.join(timeout=1.0)
446	        self._reconnect_thread = None
447	
448	    def _reconnect_loop(self) -> None:
449	        while not self._reconnect_stop.is_set():
450	            if self._reconnect_stop.wait(RECONNECT_INTERVAL):
451	                return
452	            with self._lock:
453	                want = self._port_name
454	                owned = self._owned
455	                connected = self._connected
456	            if want is None or not owned or connected:
457	                continue
458	            try:
459	                ser = serial.Serial(
460	                    port=want,
461	                    baudrate=ACTUATOR_BAUDRATE,
462	                    bytesize=serial.EIGHTBITS,
463	                    parity=serial.PARITY_NONE,
464	                    stopbits=serial.STOPBITS_ONE,
465	                    timeout=0.1,
466	                )
467	            except (serial.SerialException, OSError):
468	                continue
469	            with self._lock:
470	                if self._port_name != want or not self._owned:
471	                    try:
472	                        ser.close()
473	                    except Exception:
474	                        pass
475	                    continue
476	                self._ser = ser
477	                self._connected = True
478	            log.info("actuator: reconnected on %s", want)
479	            self._notify()
480
